promises.title: Mancherial district and Bellampally revenue division
promises.promise_text: The first Telangana government reorganised districts for closer administration. G.O. Ms. No. 222, Revenue Department, dated 11 October 2016, notified Mancherial district with effect from that day, including a new Bellampally revenue division and new mandals Bheemaram, Naspur, Hajipur and Kannepally.

delivery.summary: The same government order is the notification. Mancherial district, the Bellampally revenue division, and the new mandals took effect on 11 October 2016.

promises.title: Rythu Bandhu raised to Rs 10,000 per acre a year
promises.promise_text: The December 2018 TRS manifesto promised to raise Rythu Bandhu investment support from Rs 8,000 per acre per year to Rs 10,000. The scheme itself had begun in 2018 at Rs 4,000 per acre per season.

delivery.summary: By 1 June 2022 the scheme was being described at Rs 10,000 per acre per year. A later account counted 11 payment rounds under BRS before Congress renamed the support Rythu Bharosa. The later scheme is a separate row.

promises.title: Government medical college for Mancherial
promises.promise_text: In June 2021 the state sanctioned a government medical college for Mancherial, one of eight new colleges. Local TRS leaders described it as a long-standing district demand. The college site lists an intake of 100 MBBS seats a year from the 2022-23 year.

delivery.summary: On 15 November 2022 the district collector said the Chief Minister had inaugurated classes. Teaching had started. This record does not confirm that a permanent campus building was finished.

promises.title: Chennur Lift Irrigation Scheme
promises.promise_text: Administrative sanction on 23 April 2022 for a scheme to lift 10 tmc from the Kaleshwaram system, irrigate 90,000 acres, and supply drinking water to 103 villages, at Rs 1,658 crore. The 2022 report split the ayacut across Chennur, Kotapalli, Bheemaram, Jaipur and Mandamarri.

delivery.summary: On 17 May 2024 Telangana Today reported that construction had not started and the survey had not been taken up. A foundation was reported as laid on a June 8, year not stated in that report. This register has no later public update.

promises.title: Junior colleges at Tandur and Nennal
promises.promise_text: During the 2023 Assembly election, Congress candidate Gaddam Vinod promised junior colleges at Thandur and Nennal mandal centres. He won the Bellampalli seat. The Board of Intermediate Education sanctioned the colleges in 2025.

delivery.summary: As of 14 June 2026 the colleges were sanctioned on paper and land had not been identified. Students from Thandur and Nennal were still travelling to Bellampalli and Mancherial.

promises.title: Rythu Bharosa in Mancherial district
promises.promise_text: Rythu Bharosa farm investment support in Mancherial district. Officials told Telangana Today that 1.52 lakh farmers received Rs 198.13 crore in the 2025 Vanakalam season, and 1.56 lakh farmers received Rs 125.95 crore in the Yasangi season.

delivery.summary: As of 13 June 2026 two instalments of Rs 6,000 per acre had been released (22 March and 22 April), and farmers said the benefit was still limited and the full season amount was pending as Vanakalam work began.

promises.title: Chennur works for the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu
promises.promise_text: On 15 September 2026 the Energy and Mines Minister said about Rs 70 crore had been sanctioned for Chennur ahead of the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu: ghats, approach roads and lighting. He laid the foundation for a Pushkar Ghat. The same briefing cited Rs 8 crore for bathing ghats, Rs 17 crore for the Shiva temple, Rs 1.2 crore in DMFT funds for 20 shops, and Rs 30 crore under AMRUT.

delivery.summary: Foundation stone of the Pushkar Ghat was laid on 15 September 2026. The report describes the works as sanctioned and being taken up, not as completed.

promises.title: Mancherial internal road widening and underground drainage
promises.promise_text: Widening of internal roads was taken up in January 2026 at an estimated Rs 78 crore, with an underground drainage system. Named stretches include Bellampalli Chowrasta to the railway station, IB Chowk to Srinivas Gardens, the station to the College Road flyover, Vishwanatha Temple to Venkateshwara Theatre, and Bhashyam School to the police station.

delivery.summary: On 1 June 2026 the work was reported delayed. The mayor said roads were planned for completion in six months and drainage in a month or two. Traders reported trenches, debris and loss of business.
